commands.openPair: Open pair: side by side, attachment left, note right (created if missing)
commands.backfill: Create missing notes for all groups

notices.noGroup: "${file}" does not belong to any mapping group.
notices.noNote: Group "${group}" has note creation turned off — nothing to refresh.
notices.noteBlocked: A different note already occupies that path for "${file}".
notices.auxiliaryMatched: "${file}" matched "${note}" as an auxiliary file and was moved into its folder.
notices.auxiliaryUnmatched: "${file}" has the auxiliary prefix but matched no note — left where it is.
notices.noProperties: "${note}" has no frontmatter properties and the template has no keys either — nothing to compare.
notices.sourceRepairRequired: Found candidate note "${note}", but it has no matching source. Use the batch preview to confirm the relation.
notices.templateMissing: Template "${path}" not found (group ${group}); used the built-in fields.
notices.templaterSkipped: Skipped ${count} Templater block(s) in the template — this plugin does not run them.

unbind.title: Unbind resource
unbind.subtitle: Select the resources to remove from the source of "${note}". This changes only source, never the title, body, or files.

backfill.nothingToChange: There are no pending changes. Resources with a source relation or an existing item folder are skipped.
backfill.previewSubtitle: ${items} resource(s), ${changes} filesystem or property change(s). Nothing is moved or written before confirmation.
backfill.complete: Batch complete: ${created} processed, ${skipped} failed or changed since preview.

upgrade.complete: ${group}: updated ${notesUpdated} note(s), added ${propertiesAdded} propert(y/ies). Only filled what was empty — nothing already there was touched.

refresh.title: Refresh metadata
refresh.subtitle: Pick one side per property for "${note}". Unselected rows stay as they are.
refresh.noChanges: The extracted metadata matches the note. Nothing to choose.

sections.mapping: Field mapping (one table for the whole vault)

language.name: Interface language
language.desc: Command names change language only after Obsidian reloads the plugin.

templateFolders.name: Extra template folders
templateFolders.detected: Detected: ${folders}. Add more comma-separated paths here.
templateFolders.none: No template plugin folder detected. Add comma-separated paths here.

mapping.desc: Decides which metadata source fills which property name — configured once for the whole vault. source is the fixed resource-relation property and cannot be renamed here. Leave another name empty to skip it; keys absent from the template are not written. Inputs fuzzy-match template properties.

kinds.vault: From the vault and the file itself

groups.desc: A group maps one attachment folder to one note folder, with its own extensions, template and naming. Groups may nest — the most specific attachment folder wins.
groups.empty: No groups yet. Add one to start mapping attachments to notes.

group.name: Group name
group.removeConfirm: Delete the group "${name}"? Notes already created stay where they are.

layout.name: Layout
layout.sidecar: Sidecar (attachment stays put, note is separate)
layout.folder: Folder (a new folder holds the attachment and the note together)

desc.sidecar: The attachment stays in the attachments folder; the note lives in a mirrored path under the notes folder. The two recognize each other through the frontmatter link.
desc.folder: A new folder, named like the note, is created under the notes folder; the attachment is moved into it and the note lives beside it. Existing pairs are recognized only through source; deleting a resource never deletes its note.

createNoteFile.name: Create a note for new attachments
createNoteFile.desc: Off: folding into a folder still happens (a same-named folder is created and the attachment moved in), but no note is created and no metadata is extracted — for material that just needs a folder of its own, not a note with frontmatter. Template, link format, embedding and PDF/DOI extraction are hidden while this is off.

auxiliaryPrefix.name: Auxiliary file prefixes
auxiliaryPrefix.desc: Comma separated, e.g. cn_, zh_, slides_. A file is matched by its name after the prefix against an existing note or source resource, moved into the same folder, and appended to the source list. No match leaves it in place. Empty disables this.

attachmentsFolder.name: Attachments folder
attachmentsFolder.desc: Files placed here get a note.

notesFolder.name: Notes folder
notesFolder.desc: Where the notes are created. May sit above the attachments folder.

extensions.name: Watched extensions
extensions.desc: Comma separated, e.g. .pdf, .epub. Only these files are picked up.

template.name: Template file
template.desc: The template's frontmatter decides which properties this group's notes get. The body is copied as-is, but Templater code in it is not executed. Empty means the built-in minimal field set.
template.builtin: No template — built-in fields: source / title / author / created / updated
template.keys: Template keys: ${keys} (✓ = a source is mapped to it)
template.noKeys: This template has no frontmatter, so no properties would be written.

mirror.name: Mirror subfolders
mirror.desc: Recreate the attachment's subfolder tree under the notes folder.

noteName.name: Note name
noteName.desc: Variables: {{basename}} (no extension), {{name}} (with extension), {{ext}}. Also {{year}} and {{title}}: when the file name follows Zotero's common "Author - Year - Title" pattern, these are parsed back out of it (pure string matching, no file read) — e.g. {{year}}-{{title}} for "2023-Title". Files that do not match get an empty {{year}}; {{title}} falls back to the full file name. If the resulting name is taken by another attachment, the extension is added back.

linkTemplate.name: source link format
linkTemplate.desc: Wikilink format written to source; defaults to [[{{name}}]] (with extension). Avoid [[{{basename}}]]: when the note has the same basename, that link resolves to the note itself — the plugin adds the extension back if detected. Use [[{{path}}]] for duplicate resource names.

embed.name: Embed the attachment
embed.desc: Append an embed of the attachment to the note body. Off by default.

name.sidecar: Create a note when an attachment is added
name.folder: Fold new attachments into a folder automatically

desc.sidecar: Off: only the manual commands create notes.
desc.folder: Off: fold into a folder only via commands such as "open pair". On: a new attachment is moved into its own folder and its note created as soon as it lands.

syncUpdated.name: Keep the updated property in sync
syncUpdated.desc: Refreshes it when the attachment changes on disk. Never adds the property to a note that lacks it.

pdfExtraction.name: Read PDF metadata
pdfExtraction.desc: Title, author, subject, keywords, dates, producer and page count.

doiLookup.name: Look up DOI / ISBN online
doiLookup.desc: Finds an identifier in the PDF metadata (and, if Obsidian's PDF engine is reachable, on the first pages), then queries CrossRef or Open Library.

sanitize.name: Sanitize list values
sanitize.desc: Strip characters Obsidian rejects in tags from list fields such as keywords.

backfill.name: Create missing notes
backfill.desc: Scan this group's attachments and create the notes that do not exist yet.

upgrade.name: Align all notes to the current template
upgrade.desc: Scans this group's existing notes: properties the template now calls for that a note is missing get filled from the current mapping. Fills only what is empty — never touches a property that already has a value, never removes anything the template does not know about. Good for after the template or a mapping name changes and old notes need to catch up.

path.name: File path
path.desc: Full vault path. Also used to prove which attachment a note belongs to.

fileNameYear.name: Year (from file name)
fileNameYear.desc: Parsed from a "Author - Year - Title" style file name — no network, no file read. Maps to year by default, and is tried before the online lookup: if the file name already carries the year, there is no need to go online. Empty when the name does not match.

fileNameTitle.name: Title (from file name)
fileNameTitle.desc: Same parsing, the title part; falls back to the full file name when the pattern does not match. Not mapped by default — set a property name if you want it.

pdfTitle.name: Title
pdfTitle.desc: PDF title, falling back to the file name.

pdfKeywords.name: Keywords
pdfKeywords.desc: PDF keywords, written as a list.

pdfCreated.name: PDF created
pdfCreated.desc: Creation date recorded inside the PDF.

pdfModified.name: PDF modified
pdfModified.desc: Modification date recorded inside the PDF.

pdfCreator.name: PDF creator
pdfCreator.desc: Application that produced the original document.

lookupTitle.name: Title (online)
lookupTitle.desc: Title from CrossRef or Open Library. May share a property with the PDF title; a value found in the PDF is not overwritten.

lookupAuthor.name: Author (online)
lookupAuthor.desc: Authors from CrossRef or Open Library.

lookupYear.name: Year (online)
lookupYear.desc: Publication year from the online lookup — a fallback for when fileNameYear cannot be parsed.
